To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
developmental features can be considered biomakers of coevolution during the evolutionary process, which can be used to reconstruct the environmental changes during evolution.
the evolution of life is a coevolution between life and environment and the evolution of life can be studied using the biomarkers of the past.
ontogenetic changes in susceptibility/resistance of organisms to physiochemical agents can be considered biomarker of environmental changes during evolution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the hypothesis that ontogenic biomarkers can be considered as the evolutionary record of the past at the level of living organisms.
the hypothesis that developmental features of living organisms reflect environmental changes during Earth’s history and that evoecotoxicology can provide new insights into the evolutionary process.
the hypothesis that the evolution of life forms and the development of organisms are closely related to the evolution of the environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
evoecotoxicology provides an opportunity to reconstruct the history of life and the Earth.
the ontogeny reflects the phylogeny.
the evolutionary history of life forms is recorded at different developmental stages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evolution of life is a process of adaptation of living organisms to the physicochemical environment.

evoecotoxicology is a new field of research, which is based on the idea that ontogenetic changes in susceptibility of organisms to environmental stressors are biomarkers of evolutionary changes in the environment and life form features.
the evolutionary process can be considered a coevolution of living organisms and physico-chemical agents.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the evolution of living organisms is a process of adaptation to environmental changes, and that the ontogenetic features and stage-dependent sensitivity of living organisms are the record of the past.
the evolution of organisms and their environment is a coevolutionary process.
the ontogenetic features and stage-dependent resistance to physico-chemical agents of living organisms can reflect the history of evolution.
